newsitem.title: PERU: Venezuela's 1997 inflation target attainable - Casas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's 1997 inflation target attainable - Casas.

text.p: The Venezuelan government's 1997 inflation target of between 30 percent and 35 percent is attainable provided a tight rein is kept on public spending, Venezuelan Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said Wednesday.

"I think it (the inflation target) is attainable, but, of course, with very tight discipline in spending," Casas told Reuters in an interview during a meeting of central bank officials from the Americas and Spain.
Casas welcomed a recent fall in monthly inflation to 1.6 percent in March -- Venezuela's lowest monthly rate in five years.
But he stressed the importance of creating a "Macroeconomic Stabilization Fund" as soon as possible, to store windfall revenues from high oil prices.
The stabilization fund would prevent these revenues from feeding into current government expenditure and pushing up inflation, he said.
Casas also urged caution in the current debate over a new minimum salary.
The government is considering raising the minimum monthly wage to between 67,000 bolivars ($140.5) and 90,000 bolivars from 53,000 bolivars at present.
Casas warned that a figure near 90,000 bolivars could blow the government's inflation goal.
"I think we have to be very careful with what we do because if not what we gain through controlling inflation could be lost," he said.
